slides.title: Deque Memory Layout
slides.prompt: How is memory internally stored in std::deque compared to std::vector?
options: A series of fixed-size contiguous memory chunks managed by an array of pointers
A single continuous block of heap memory
A doubly linked list of individual nodes
slides.correctAnswer: A series of fixed-size contiguous memory chunks managed by an array of pointers

slides.title: Random Access Support
slides.prompt: Does std::deque support random access indexing using operator[]?
options: Yes, with O(1) constant time complexity (though slightly slower than std::vector due to pointer indirection)
No, random access is not supported
Yes, but access takes O(N) linear time
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, with O(1) constant time complexity (though slightly slower than std::vector due to pointer indirection)

slides.title: Contiguous Memory Comparison
slides.prompt: Why can't std::deque elements be passed directly to C-style APIs requiring raw array pointers?
